Assess an R package's security vulnerabilities from package name and version

Source: R/generate_security_vulnerabilities.R
generate_security_vulnerabilities.Rd

This standalone function retrieves known security vulnerabilities for `pkg_name` and `pkg_ver` from the Open Source Vulnerabilities database.

Usage

generate_security_vulnerabilities(pkg_name, pkg_ver = NULL, ecosystem = "CRAN")

Arguments

pkg_name

A character string specifying the name of the package to assess.

pkg_ver

A character string specifying the version of the package to assess. Default is `NULL`, which assesses every known version.

ecosystem

A character string specifying the OSV ecosystem the package belongs to. Default is `"CRAN"`.

Value

A list of known security vulnerabilities for the package, with columns `pkg_name`, `pkg_ver`, `ecosystem`, `id`, `summary`, `details`, `introduced`, `fixed`, `modified`, and `published`. An empty data frame with the same columns is returned when there are no known vulnerabilities.

Details

See the `security vulnerabilities` vignette for more details on the ecosystems

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

results <- generate_security_vulnerabilities(
  "commonmark",
  pkg_ver = "1.7"
)

print(results)

results_multi <- c("haven", "commonmark") |>
  rlang::set_names() |>
  purrr::map(\(x) {
    res <- generate_security_vulnerabilities(x)
    
    # 1. Convert NULL to NA so it has a valid size of 1
    if (is.null(res$pkg_ver)) res$pkg_ver <- NA_character_
    
    # 2. Explicitly wrap the vulnerabilities object in a list to form a list-column
    res$vulnerabilities <- list(res$vulnerabilities)
    
    tibble::as_tibble_row(res)
  }) |>
  purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "pkg")

print(results_multi)
} # }
